source_refs.note: Topic 22.2.5 with the worked example (PDF 195-196). The book's step 4 says 'subtract the maximum value from the minimum value'; the calculation it shows subtracts the minimum from the maximum, as the lesson says.

blocks.text: The range is the simplest measure of spread: the difference between the largest and smallest values, range = Xmax - Xmin. A larger range means the data are more spread out; a smaller range means they are clustered around a central value.

Example: the ages 25, 20, 22, 30, 42, 45 and 50. Ordered: 20, 22, 25, 30, 42, 45, 50. The greatest value is 50 and the smallest 20, so subtracting the minimum from the maximum gives range = 50 - 20 = 30.

blocks.prompt: Why can the range be misleading?
blocks.explanation: It uses only the two extreme values, so a single unusual value can make it very large even if most data are close together.
